title: Gesture fallthrough and ARIA concise profiles for streaming time-series
creator: Lena Cho
comments: 2026-02-18 - Initial ticket: define UX for gesture fallthrough (legend -> chart) and lightweight ARIA announcements for streaming charts. Goal: reduce noise for screen reader users while preserving discoverability.

2026-02-23 - Design spike done: created three announcement modes: concise (one-line summary per stream batch), delta (announce changes above threshold), and verbose (full point readout). Prototype in Figma: attached. Decided to default to concise for high-frequency feeds.

2026-02-28 - Engineering sync: Eng prefers event-driven announcer that can be toggled by route and respects batching windows. Agreed on a 800ms debounce for live streams; will expose config via chart props: announceMode, announceWindowMs.

2026-03-03 - Accessibility review (Axe + manual): recommended minimizing DOM live region updates and using aria-atomic=false with aria-relevant="text" in concise mode. Also suggested an opt-in detailed-reader API for assistive tech labs.
2026-03-05 - PM feedback: add telemetry tags to measure announcement frequency and dropped announcements. PM asked to document migration notes for apps currently using legacy announce strategy.

2026-03-09 - Design decision: implement default concise summary string pattern: "SeriesName: current 2.3k, Δ +120 since last update". For threshold-based delta mode, thresholds are configurable per-series via data attributes. Chose aria-live=polite for concise, assertive only for critical threshold breaches.

2026-03-10 - Next steps: prototype implementation in a small app (ENG spike), run 5 internal screen-reader tests, measure announce latency on staging dashboard. Prepare a short migration guide and an API doc for custom announcer handlers. Figma link updated with interaction notes.
notes: Trade-offs: strong batching reduces TTS spam but increases time-to-announce. We picked 800ms as balanced default; team can tune per-workload. Performance tuning includes using a single offscreen region element and string diffing to avoid reflow. For low-power devices we will fall back to succinct numeric badges instead of TTS.
acceptance_criteria: Default concise mode reduces announcement rate by >=60% vs legacy per-point announce (measured in staging)
Screen-reader testers (NVDA, VoiceOver) confirm no blocking of core chart keyboard flows
Engineering implements announceMode and announceWindowMs props with docs and feature flag
Migration guide published and linked in PR
